title: watch() Lazy Source vs watchEffect() Flush Timing (pre, post, sync)

progressiveExplaining.eli5: `watch` is like a detective assigned to follow one specific suspect (e.g. only watch `userId`). It does nothing until that suspect moves, and it tells you both their old and new locations. `watchEffect` is a security guard in a room who watches everything happening right now, runs immediately on day one, and re-runs whenever anything in the room changes.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `watch(source, callback)` is lazy by default: it tracks explicit dependencies, provides `(newValue, oldValue)`, and only runs when the source changes. `watchEffect(callback)` runs immediately on initialization, automatically tracks any reactive dependencies read inside its body, but does not provide the previous value. The `flush` option (`'pre'`, `'post'`, `'sync'`) controls when the watcher callback executes relative to DOM updates.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `watch` and `watchEffect` are wrappers over `ReactiveEffect`. `flush: 'pre'` (default) runs watcher callbacks *before* component DOM updates; `flush: 'post'` (or `watchPostEffect`) runs callbacks *after* component DOM updates (essential for reading updated template refs or DOM geometry); `flush: 'sync'` (or `watchSyncEffect`) executes synchronously on every mutation, bypassing the scheduler microtask batch.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When a signal/ref mutates, `trigger()` schedules the effect in the scheduler queue (`queueJob`). If `flush: 'pre'`, the job is placed in the pre-flush queue evaluated before the component update effect. If `flush: 'post'`, the job is placed in the post-flush queue evaluated after `patch()`. If `flush: 'sync'`, the effect's `scheduler` simply calls `effect.run()` immediately within the mutating call stack.

rosettaStone.react: `useEffect` with dependency array (similar to post-flush watcher).

codeComparison.title: Explicit watch() vs Automatic watchEffect() with Post-DOM Flush
codeComparison.summary: `watch` requires explicit sources and previous values; `watchEffect` auto-tracks and can wait for DOM updates with `flush: 'post'`.

legacyOrBad.label: Accidental Pre-Flush DOM Read
legacyOrBad.snippet: watchEffect(() => { readDom(el.value); }); // ❌ Reads stale DOM before render

fullFile.code:
<script setup>
import { ref, watchEffect } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);
const buttonRef = ref(null);

// ❌ OLD: Default flush is 'pre' (runs BEFORE DOM updates),
// so buttonRef.value.textContent returns the STALE count value!
watchEffect(() => {
  if (buttonRef.value) {
    console.log('DOM Text:', buttonRef.value.textContent); // Stale!
  }
  console.log('Count:', count.value);
});
</script>

<template>
  <button ref="buttonRef" @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>
</template>

modernOrGood.label: watchPostEffect for Fresh DOM Access
modernOrGood.snippet: watchPostEffect(() => { readDom(buttonRef.value); }); // ✅ NEW: Guaranteed updated DOM

fullFile.code:
<script setup>
import { ref, watchPostEffect, watch } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);
const buttonRef = ref(null);

// ✅ NEW: watchPostEffect (flush: 'post') runs AFTER the DOM has updated.
watchPostEffect(() => {
  if (buttonRef.value) {
    console.log('Updated DOM Text:', buttonRef.value.textContent); // Fresh!
  }
});

// ✅ Use watch() when you need both (newVal, oldVal) or lazy execution:
watch(count, (newVal, oldVal) => {
  console.log(`Count changed from ${oldVal} to ${newVal}`);
});
</script>

<template>
  <button ref="buttonRef" @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>
</template>

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `flush: 'pre'`, `flush: 'post'`, and `flush: 'sync'`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of Vue's render queue and DOM synchronization lifecycle.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer:
- **`flush: 'pre'` (Default)**: Watcher callback runs before the component's DOM patch phase. Multiple state updates are batched into a single pre-render run.
- **`flush: 'post'` (`watchPostEffect`)**: Watcher callback runs *after* the component's DOM patch phase. Use this whenever reading template refs or measuring DOM dimensions.
- **`flush: 'sync'` (`watchSyncEffect`)**: Watcher runs immediately and synchronously the instant the ref/reactive property mutates, bypassing batching (use with caution as it can cause performance bottlenecks).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Accessing template refs inside a default `watchEffect` on initial run will yield `null` because the component has not mounted yet.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you watch a nested property of a `reactive()` object using `watch()`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of getter source functions in `watch()`.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: You **must pass a getter function**: `watch(() => state.user.name, (newName, oldName) => { ... })`. Passing the property directly (`watch(state.user.name, ...)` ) passes a static string or primitive, which Vue cannot track.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Passing `state.property` directly into `watch` throws a runtime warning and will never trigger the callback.
